speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where your wrist pain is located and what activities make it worse. To help me narrow this down, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or a specific injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis (with possible superimposed osteoarthritis of the first CMC joint).

I suspect the pain radiating to the elbow is referred from the thumb base, but I need to rule out a fracture from that fall six months ago. REQUEST TEST: X-ray of the right wrist and thumb. REQUEST IMAGES: Please return images of the right wrist and thumb X-rays.
